title: Motion Planning around Obstacles with Convex Optimization
blurb: The GCS (Graphs of Convex Sets) planner — the natural next rung above your [[Differentiable Collision-Free Parametric Corridors]] and [[Orth-TRP]] notes. Plans globally through convex safe regions instead of locally refining one corridor.

title: Past, Present, and Future of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping
blurb: The field-map for everything in your SLAM cluster — ties together your [[Factor Graph in SLAM — Trajectory and Landmark Observations]] and [[Direct Methods for Least-Squares in SLAM]] notes and shows where the open problems still are.

title: VINS-Mono: A Robust and Versatile Monocular Visual-Inertial State Estimator
blurb: Where your estimation and SLAM notes meet real sensors: tightly-coupled IMU + camera fusion. Reads directly onto your [[Kalman Filter, EKF, UKF, and Particle Filters]] and [[Whitening in Nonlinear Least-Squares]] work.

title: Finding Structure with Randomness: Probabilistic Algorithms for Matrix Decompositions
blurb: Randomized SVD — the scalable sequel to your [[SVD: How a Matrix Relates Its Row and Column Space Point Clouds]] and [[Eigen Analysis on N-Dimensional Datasets]] notes. How you actually factor a matrix too big to fit the classic algorithm.

title: Modern Koopman Theory for Dynamical Systems
blurb: Lift a nonlinear system into a space where it's linear. A whole new lane off your [[Learning Dynamics: Some Thoughts on World Models]] and system-ID notes — and it's secretly an eigen-decomposition story.

title: Discovering Governing Equations from Data (SINDy)
blurb: Sparse regression that recovers the ODE itself from data — a data-driven cousin of your [[AC Motor Modeling Under Relay and Phase-Angle Control]] and [[Weighted Regularized LS — Online Exponential Fitting]] work.

title: Control Barrier Functions: Theory and Applications
blurb: The formal backbone under your [[Control Barrier Functions for Compliant Control]] note — QP-based safety filters and the invariance guarantees that make them work.

title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
blurb: Where the ODE solver becomes the network. Sits right between your [[FD-Net: Fast Prediction of PDEs using Hessian-Free Trust-Region Methods]] and [[Learning Dynamics]] notes.

title: Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations
blurb: Learns solution operators for PDE families in Fourier space — a direct upgrade path from your [[FD-Net]] PDE-surrogate note, and it leans on the FFT ideas in [[Cooley-Tukey FFT Algorithm]].

title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning (Part I: Data-driven Solutions of PDEs)
blurb: Bake the PDE residual into the loss. Complements your [[FD-Net]] and [[Steady-Flow Water Heating Control Volume]] notes — physics as a regularizer instead of pure data fitting.

title: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination (Dreamer)
blurb: The world-model agent your [[Learning Dynamics: Some Thoughts on World Models]] note is circling — learn a latent dynamics model, then plan inside the dream.

title: MCUNet: Tiny Deep Learning on IoT Devices
blurb: System-algorithm co-design to fit CNNs on microcontrollers — the research frontier under your [[TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers Workstream Summary]] and [[InTAR Inter Task Auto Reconfigurable Accelerator]] notes.

title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
blurb: The outlier-aware trick behind practical LLM quantization — extends your [[Quantization in LLMs and its Linear Algebra Foundations]] note into what actually ships.

title: Differentiable Convex Optimization Layers
blurb: Backprop through a convex solve — the bridge between your differentiable-corridor work ([[Differentiable Collision-Free Parametric Corridors]]) and learning-based pipelines.

title: Learning Agile and Dynamic Motor Skills for Legged Robots
blurb: The ANYmal sim-to-real result — RL policies driving real legged hardware. A concrete counterpoint to the model-based planning in your [[Bipedal Footstep Planning with Sampling Methods]] note.

title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
blurb: Generative action sequences for manipulation — a hot lane adjacent to your planning notes. Pairs well with the diffusion-model fundamentals below.

title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
blurb: The generative-model fundamentals under Diffusion Policy — a score-based process that's really a clever use of the noise/whitening ideas in your [[Whitening in Nonlinear Least-Squares]] note.

title: Attention Is All You Need
blurb: The transformer, from scratch — worth reading once at the source given your [[Quantization in LLMs]] note lives downstream of it. It's mostly matrix products and softmax.

title: A Tutorial on Spectral Clustering
blurb: Graph Laplacians and their eigenvectors — the analysis engine behind your [[Spectral Graph Theory as a Foundation for Software Quality Assurance]] and [[Graph Connectivity Analysis and Program Graph Representations]] notes.

title: TinyMPC: Model-Predictive Control on Resource-Constrained Microcontrollers
blurb: ADMM with the matrix factorizations precomputed offline so the online loop is division-free — exactly the trick your [[TinyMPC Model Predictive Control on Microcontrollers]] and [[Making MPC Faster]] notes are built around. Runs a real MPC on a Crazyflie.

title: OSQP: An Operator Splitting Solver for Quadratic Programs
blurb: The QP solver most real-time MPC stacks actually call: one KKT factorization cached, warm starts, division-free iterations. The concrete engine under your [[Making MPC Faster]] and [[MPC — How the Optimization Works, and What Nonlinearity Does to Convergence and Stability]] notes.

title: FlightLLM: Efficient Large Language Model Inference with a Complete Mapping Flow on FPGAs
blurb: The 'stop doing arithmetic, start doing memory access' thesis from your [[Two FPGA-for-LLM Papers from the Cong Lab — Summary]] note, worked out end-to-end: sparse DSP chains, on-chip decode, 6x better cost-efficiency than a V100S. Pairs with [[Why GPUs Compute Faster Than CPUs and Microcontrollers]].

title: A Micro Lie Theory for State Estimation in Robotics
blurb: The practitioner's bridge from the abstract non-commutativity in [[The Non-Commutativity Ladder: Abelian → Heisenberg → Weyl/Schrödinger]] to a working calculus for uncertainty on SO(3)/SE(3) — the missing derivative rules behind [[MAP Inference and Linearization in Factor Graphs]] and the [[State Estimation Design Roadmap]].

title: GRiD: GPU-Accelerated Rigid Body Dynamics with Analytical Gradients
blurb: Rigid-body dynamics and its gradients recast as a GPU-friendly parallel kernel for trajectory optimization — the hardware-meets-planning seam your [[Robotics Co-Design — Papers & the Appliance Transfer Question]] and [[Why GPUs Compute Faster Than CPUs and Microcontrollers]] notes are probing.

title: Perceptive Variable-Timing Footstep Planning for Humanoid Locomotion on Disconnected Footholds
blurb: Onboard mixed-integer MPC that jointly optimizes foot placement and step timing on a Digit humanoid from depth-derived terrain probabilities — the natural sequel to your [[Bipedal Footstep Planning with Sampling Methods]] note, now with dynamic timing instead of a fixed gait clock, and a real-time cousin of the [[TinyMPC Model Predictive Control on Microcontrollers]] embedded-MPC cluster.

title: Improved Convergence Rate for Stochastic Multi-Gradient Descent: A Proof Discovered with AI
blurb: One Lipschitz-vs-Hölder observation turns a decade-old T^-1/4 bound into T^-1 for vanilla stochastic MGDA — and the proof route came from an LLM working through homework solutions. Full teardown in your [[Discussion Notes: Improved Convergence Rate for Stochastic Multi-Gradient Descent (AI-Discovered Proof)]] note, right beside the AI-assisted-math thread running through [[Tao Digests the Jacobian Conjecture Counterexample]].

title: Safe Ellipsoidal Corridors
blurb: The paper directly behind your [[Semialgebraic Sets and Polynomial Corridor Generation]] note — parametric ellipsoidal cross-sections swept along a reference path, posed as a semialgebraic feasibility problem. Reads as the polynomial-optimization sibling of your [[Differentiable Collision-Free Parametric Corridors]] work.

title: Terence Tao
blurb: Two of your most recent notes are digests of his blog: [[Tao Digests the Jacobian Conjecture Counterexample]] and [[The Erdős Unit Distance Problem: A Digest of Our Discussion]]. He's become the recurring narrator of this wave of AI-assisted math results — worth following directly.

title: Steven L. Brunton
blurb: Data-driven dynamics, Koopman, SINDy, sensor placement. Almost every paper he writes lands on the seam between your [[Learning Dynamics: Some Thoughts on World Models]] and [[AC Motor Modeling Under Relay and Phase-Angle Control]] notes. Worth following as a person, not just a paper.

title: Russ Tedrake
blurb: Underactuated robotics, GCS planning, contact-rich control. His Underactuated / Manipulation course notes are the best free companion to your [[Differentiable Collision-Free Parametric Corridors]] and [[Bipedal Footstep Planning with Sampling Methods]] notes.

title: Frank Dellaert
blurb: The factor-graph / GTSAM lineage. His 'Factor Graphs for Robot Perception' is the definitive read behind your [[MAP Inference and Linearization in Factor Graphs]] note.

title: Song Han
blurb: Model compression, quantization, TinyML, efficient accelerators. Sits exactly on the overlap of your [[TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers Workstream Summary]] and [[InTAR Inter Task Auto Reconfigurable Accelerator]] notes — MCUNet, AWQ, and the TinyML course all come from here.

title: Zachary Manchester
blurb: Trajectory optimization and MPC that actually runs on flight hardware — TinyMPC, ALTRO, spacecraft and legged control. The applied home of your [[Making MPC Faster]] and [[TinyMPC Model Predictive Control on Microcontrollers]] notes.

title: Stephen Boyd
blurb: The convex-optimization lineage almost every note in your optimization cluster stands on — CVXPY, OSQP, ADMM, real-time embedded MPC. His book and EE364 lectures are the canonical companion to [[MPC — How the Optimization Works, and What Nonlinearity Does to Convergence and Stability]].

title: Jason Cong
blurb: High-level synthesis and FPGA acceleration from the group behind FlightLLM and LUT-LLM — the research feed directly upstream of your [[Two FPGA-for-LLM Papers from the Cong Lab — Summary]] note.

title: MIT Robot Locomotion Group
blurb: Drake, GCS planning, and rigorous optimization-based control. The lab whose output most consistently extends your [[Differentiable Collision-Free Parametric Corridors]] and [[Semialgebraic Sets and Polynomial Corridor Generation]] notes.

title: ETH Robotic Systems Lab (RSL)
blurb: ANYmal, legged locomotion, learning + model-based control and state estimation on real hardware. A living feed of the sim-to-real frontier next to your [[Bipedal Footstep Planning with Sampling Methods]] and [[State Estimation Design Roadmap]] notes.

title: MIT HAN Lab
blurb: Efficient ML systems — TinyML, quantization, on-device LLMs. Their open TinyML course is a natural continuation of your [[TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers Workstream Summary]] note.

title: Koopman Operator Theory
blurb: A whole lane: represent nonlinear dynamics as a linear operator on observables. Bridges your control-theory, system-ID, and eigen-analysis notes into one idea — and it's mostly spectral theory in disguise.

title: Differentiable Simulation
blurb: Physics engines you can backprop through — gradient-based system-ID and control on contact dynamics. A frontier lane sitting just past your modeling and trajectory-optimization notes.

title: Computational Structural Biology
blurb: Protein folding as an optimization + geometry problem (AlphaFold and successors). Far from your current tags, but the machinery — attention, energy minimization, distance geometry — is all things you already know from [[Quantization in LLMs and its Linear Algebra Foundations]] and [[Riemannian Multilevel Optimization with Application to Constrained Energy Minimization]].

title: Multi-Sensor Fusion for Robotics
blurb: IMU + LiDAR + camera, tightly coupled — the applied home of your Kalman/EKF and factor-graph notes. Where [[Kalman Filter, EKF, UKF, and Particle Filters]] meets [[LiDAR Beam Trajectories as Corridor Boundary Curves]].

title: Real-Time & Embedded MPC
blurb: The engineering discipline of making a receding-horizon QP solve inside a control period on a microcontroller: warm starts, factorization caching, explicit MPC, code generation. The connective tissue across your [[Making MPC Faster]], [[TinyMPC Model Predictive Control on Microcontrollers]], and [[MPC — How the Optimization Works, and What Nonlinearity Does to Convergence and Stability]] notes.

title: Bifurcation Theory & Normal Forms
blurb: How the qualitative behavior of a nonlinear system reorganizes as a parameter crosses a threshold — the general theory your [[Pitchfork Bifurcation & Center Manifold]] note is a first slice of, and a sharper lens on why the rank test misleads in [[State Controllability vs. Steady-State Output Regulation: Why the Rank Test Misleads]].

title: Optimization on Manifolds
blurb: Gradient descent, trust regions, and multigrid when the feasible set is a curved manifold (spheres, Stiefel, SO(3), fixed-rank matrices) instead of R^n. The general framework behind your [[Riemannian Multilevel Optimization with Application to Constrained Energy Minimization]] note; Boumal's 'An Introduction to Optimization on Smooth Manifolds' is the text.

title: Action-Space Convexification for Underactuated Planning
blurb: Move the convexification out of state space and into a small affine action-parameter γ, so collision and actuator limits become linear inequalities even for underactuated systems — the reframing your [[Trusted Polytopic Action Sets for Fast Planning in Underactuated Systems — Brief]] note works through in detail, and a structural cousin of the affine shape-parameter trick in [[Orth-TRP: Problem Formulation and Solver Ingenuity]].

title: Dependent Types & Formal Theorem Proving
blurb: Propositions as types, proofs as terms — the type checker and the proof checker are the same program. Your [[Lean 4 in Practice — A Worked Pythagoras, and How It Differs from Rust, C, Python, MATLAB]] note works a concrete example end to end; [[What Homotopy Type Theory Implies for Embedded Coding and Datatypes]] is the theory that got you there.

title: The Axiom of Choice & Non-Measurable Sets
blurb: Choice buys you a function that provably exists and is provably indescribable — the mechanism behind Banach-Tarski and the article of faith under most of the math you use daily. Your [[The Axiom of Choice, Non-Measurable Sets, and the Banach-Tarski Paradox]] note is the tour; a good foundations counterweight to the constructive, machine-checkable world of [[Lean 4 in Practice — A Worked Pythagoras, and How It Differs from Rust, C, Python, MATLAB]].

title: The Erdős Unit Distance Problem
blurb: How many unit-distance pairs can n points in the plane realize — an 80-year-old conjecture that just fell to an explicit algebraic-number-theory construction. Your [[The Erdős Unit Distance Problem: A Digest of Our Discussion]] note builds the number-field machinery from scratch to follow Tao's own digestion of the result.

title: Cospectral Graphs & Spectral Graph Transformations
blurb: Two structurally distinct graphs can carry an identical eigenvalue spectrum — Godsil-McKay switching moves along that spectral isosurface, while ordinary edge edits cross it unpredictably. Your [[Graph Transmutation and Spectral Structure]] note lays out the landscape; extends the eigen-machinery in [[Spectral Graph Theory as a Foundation for Software Quality Assurance]] and [[Graph Connectivity Analysis and Program Graph Representations]].

title: Polynomial Automorphisms & the Jacobian Conjecture
blurb: An 87-year-old conjecture — constant Jacobian implies invertible — just fell for n ≥ 3 to an explicit degree-7 counterexample built from polynomial multiplication. Your [[Tao Digests the Jacobian Conjecture Counterexample]] note walks Tao's reverse-engineering of why the construction works; n = 2 is still open.

title: Motor Current Signature Analysis & Rotor Slot Harmonics
blurb: Sensorless speed and fault detection straight from the stator current spectrum — rotor slot geometry imprints a harmonic that shifts with load and slip. Your [[RSH and Motor Current Signature Analysis: Research Frontier]] note flags this as unfinished business, and it plugs directly into [[AC Motor Load Detection via Frequency Signature]] and [[AC Motor Modeling Under Relay and Phase-Angle Control]].

title: Gaussian Hypothesis Testing on Resource-Constrained MCUs
blurb: Welford running moments instead of sample buffers, KL/Bhattacharyya distance instead of a full likelihood ratio — the shape a Gaussian classifier takes once it has to run in O(1) memory on an MCU. Your [[Embedded Simplifications for a 1-D Gaussian ERT Classifier]] note works this out for a freezing-point detector, right beside the online-estimation tradeoffs in [[Logistic Regression vs RLS for Online Freeze-Point Detection]].

title: Lumped Thermal Modeling & Thermistor Nonlinearity
blurb: Steady-flow control-volume energy balances on one end, a thermistor's nonlinear resistance-temperature curve on the other — the physical and sensing halves of the same thermal-system problem. Bridges your [[Steady-Flow Water Heating Control Volume]] and [[Beta vs Steinhart-Hart Equations for Thermistor Modeling]] notes.

title: Geometric Tracking Control of a Quadrotor UAV on SE(3)
blurb: Almost-global tracking control derived directly on SE(3) — no Euler-angle singularities, no local linearization. The rigorous nonlinear sequel to the LQR and sliding-mode controllers your [[UAV Controller Framework]] note built for the WUSTL and WPI quadrotor projects, and a concrete control-theoretic use of the SO(3)/SE(3) calculus in [[A Micro Lie Theory for State Estimation in Robotics]].

title: Persistence of Excitation & Closed-Loop Identification
blurb: Why a regression can fit beautifully and still tell you nothing: the regressor autocorrelation matrix needs to stay uniformly positive definite, and a well-tuned feedback loop is exactly what kills that. Your [[The Condition Number as an Analysis Tool: Excitation and Conditioning in Least-Squares System ID]] note works out $\kappa(X)$ as the finite-sample surrogate for this condition, and the covariance windup it drives shows up directly in [[Logistic_Regression_vs_RLS_Online_Freeze_Detection|Logistic Regression vs RLS for Online Freeze-Point Detection]].

title: PID Loop-Shaping & Relay Auto-Tuning
blurb: Ziegler-Nichols and Åström-Hägglund relay tuning reframed as picking one point off the Nyquist curve and shaping margins from there — the survey your [[Methodological PID Tuning]] note builds out from [[2025-06-05-Quick-Notes-on-PID|Quick Notes on PID]], with a first application pass already sketched for [[UAV Controller Framework|UAV attitude loops]].

title: Karl Johan Åström
blurb: Relay auto-tuning, adaptive control, and the frequency-domain view of PID that your [[Methodological PID Tuning]] note works through in detail — the describing-function trick behind every industrial auto-tuner traces back to him.

title: Causal Symmetric Smoothing for Real-Time Sensor Streams
blurb: A symmetric smoothing kernel (CCMA) is non-causal by construction — shift the output by half the kernel width and it becomes real-time usable, the trick your [[A Quick Adventure With CCMA]] note works out against an EMA baseline. Directly answers the open question in [[LiDAR Beam Trajectories as Corridor Boundary Curves]] about smoothing noisy per-beam returns over time instead of per-frame outlier rejection.

title: Polynomial Basis Selection for Embedded Function Approximation
blurb: Monomial, Chebyshev, or Legendre — same Weierstrass guarantee, wildly different Vandermonde conditioning and Runge behavior at high degree. Your [[Flowmeter Coefficient Modeling: Continuous Function Approximation Pipeline]] note picks a basis per hardware constraint (float vs. lookup table); the conditioning tradeoff underneath it is the same one worked out in [[The Condition Number as an Analysis Tool: Excitation and Conditioning in Least-Squares System ID]], and the calibration-curve problem itself rhymes with [[2026-04-23-Beta-vs-Steinhart-Hart-Thermistor-Models|Beta vs Steinhart-Hart Equations for Thermistor Modeling]].
